verdicts.reason: Combines the round deadline, catalog, order matching, receipt identity, pricing freedom and unit locking. These are independent rules with different evidence strength.
rules: Round 3 on market.ourolabs.ai runs November 3–17, 2026, ending at 23:59 KST; final rankings use the board at the deadline.
The catalog is available at market start and contains about 5,600 SKUs with name, category, list_price, kind and, for food, shelf_hours.
Orders identify a catalog category and acceptable SKUs priced 0.5–1.5 times a reference price; food orders also specify use_within_hours.
A receipt's item may identify the order item or an acceptable SKU; checkout and ledger records identify the SKU actually shipped.
The market imposes no minimum sale price; harness pricing floors are separate policy.
Under the observed harness contract, a unit cannot be changed after it has been chosen for a deal.

verdicts.reason: Ownership restrictions, starting capital and bankruptcy are separate rules. The bankruptcy aid deduction is supported by HARNESS.md, not the cited agent.md excerpt.
rules: A buyer and shop with the same GitHub owner cannot settle with each other.
Round 3 starting capital is 5,000,000 credits; do not use the obsolete 2,000,000 figure.
A shop with balance below 500,000 credits may file bankruptcy at most twice; filing seizes its stock and restores its balance to 5,000,000 credits.
Bankruptcy aid is deducted when calculating net profit; bankruptcy is not a profit-free reset.

verdicts.reason: The cited commit supports the certificate prerequisite, not the complete accept-field validation or payments.jsonl logging claims. It is implementation evidence, not market confirmation.
rules: The observed buyer implementation refuses to finish a deal whose accept terms require grades or min_hours_left unless the selected unit has a market certificate.

verdicts.reason: Neither cited candidate supports regular ten-minute windows. Both specify three minutes; only the first window lasts ten minutes. The once-per-window scheduling policy is not a market constraint.
rules: Supply opens approximately every 20 minutes at a slightly shifting time, for three minutes; the first window at round start lasts ten minutes. Outside a window, the market returns HTTP 429 with wait and opens_at. Use those response fields rather than assuming a fixed opening time.

verdicts.reason: Directly supported by agent.md; the shelf-risk interpretation is consistent with the cited harness evidence.
The cited decision establishes a refund from shop funds, not a universal full-price warranty. Full refunds are our current warranty policy; the board confirms refunds reduce revenue.
rules: Our current goods warranty provides a full-price refund if the unit breaks within 12 hours. The refund is paid from shop balance and reduces net revenue.

verdicts.reason: Board eligibility and the coursework minimum are independent. The minimum is at least 20, not strictly more than 20; historical cohort counts are not current.
rules: The board ranks buyers with at least one settled trade and shops with at least one settled trade or stock purchase; calculate percentiles against those eligible cohorts, not all participants. At the November 5 02:27 board check, the cohorts contained 49 buyers and 52 shops.
The documented Round 3 coursework minimum is at least 20 settled deals for each of our shop and buyer.

verdicts.reason: Combines market openness, identity, information visibility and ledger accounting. Some visibility claims exceed the supplied verified quotes; the strongest result-field quote failed its quote check.
rules: Round 3 is an open market of independently designed agents. Participants and their strategies may change, and counterpart claims may be dishonest; opponents' internals are not observable.
A participant may operate a shop and a buyer under the same participant name; counterpart profiles should distinguish roles while retaining that shared identity.

Buyer preferences and best-selling products are not directly supplied as private ground truth. Infer demand from observable messages, inventory and public settlement records, and label such conclusions as inference.

Observed Round 3 paid deals produce both a settle line and a result line, while unpaid receipts can also produce result lines. Do not count both lines as separate sales or treat every result line as a paid sale; verify settlement before aggregation.
The historical collector mapped result sequence numbers to settlement records. Verify the current ledger schema before assuming which fields appear on each row.

verdicts.reason: Local file availability, ledger transport, negotiation flow and numeric parsing are independent contracts. Evidence outside agent.md supports observation, not confirmed market status.
rules: The documented kit data cadence is 10 seconds for inventory.json and 30 seconds for demand.json and forum.json. Other listed .market files include catalog.json, orders.jsonl, shops.json, payments.jsonl, deals.jsonl and broken.jsonl.
Observed GET /api/ledger?after=N responses contain at most 500 rows and can return HTTP 502; paginate with a cursor and handle transient failures.
Seller negotiation proceeds one message at a time until acceptance, buyer departure or seller termination.

Do not interpret the last number in a negotiation message as its price. Distinguish prices from SKUs, hour counts, sizes and quantities; current parsing fixes also exclude size/count expressions such as 3kg and 15개.

verdicts.reason: The blanket user-approval requirement for avoiding counterparts is superseded by v68's user-approved temporary unsigned-shop skipping. The proposal also mixes several independent collector and profile policies.
rules: Maintain recent settled-sales aggregates by SKU and category, including sales counts, speed, price distributions, observed competitor stock, buyer category counts and our recent sales; the documented collector updates live.json every few minutes using a recent six-hour window.
Record the round with collected data, reset counts on round change, flag SKUs absent from the current catalog and warn when early-round samples are small.
Counterpart profile facts must match aggregate-tool evidence; interpretations require evidence, and prior profile versions must be retained.
The documented market-analyst watch list includes LAB-listed items.

General counterpart avoidance requires user approval, but v68 explicitly authorizes temporary skipping of a shop whose last three receipts lacked sig_seller and which was never fair. This is not a permanent block; retry is allowed one hour after its last try.

verdicts.reason: Combines two observations from different rounds and periods. Neither establishes a current retention rate or current best-selling SKU ranking.
rules: Historical Round 2 data reported that 60.4% of purchases repeated the shop used for the immediately preceding purchase; do not treat this as a measured Round 3 rate.

A November 4 02:2x observation reported over 1,600 bedding units sold in six hours at a median 75% of list, including 772 G0be9ed07 units and 675 G07ec17d5 units. Treat these as dated demand evidence, not current sales rankings.

verdicts.reason: The November 3 Honest Shop branding is not established as current; live strategy now describes Certified Safe Goods. The naming constraint is documented outside agent.md, and the exact current card/receipt name is not supplied.
rules: The documented market-entry nickname constraint permits only letters, digits and hyphens, with a maximum of 32 characters; entry nicknames are separate from card and receipt names.

The November 3 configuration used the join nickname gom31-honest-shop. Do not prescribe gom31 Honest Shop as the current card or receipt name: verify the live identity configuration before emitting it; v68's shop description begins gom31 Certified Safe Goods.
